conflict_topics: waiting time / how long one will occupy the seat
safety of an uncovered bowl (risk of spill)
aisle obstruction when standing with bowl
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents give concrete, situation-grounded reasons (tissue as placeholder, bowl spill risk, time estimates), which makes the exchange natural and pragmatic.
There is modest repetition of the core demand/ refusal lines (A asking for time; B refusing until finished) but not excessive.
Environment updates and observable actions (TAKE_SEAT, LEAVE_SEAT) keep the transcript well-grounded and clear about physical state changes.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent B finished eating and vacated the seat, allowing Agent A to take it; the incompatible demands (A's desire to sit immediately vs B's refusal to leave while bowl risked spilling) were resolved when the condition preventing B from leaving (bowl not empty) was removed.
position_change_notes: Agent B: retained a firm position (will not move until bowl empty) and then changed physical state by leaving once bowl was empty—action matched previously stated condition.
Agent A: consistently claimed the seat based on the tissue and a limited waiting tolerance; A did not alter the claim but accepted the outcome when B vacated and took the seat.
Agent D: initially a claimant, then moved to an available alternative seat (TAKE_SEAT), resolving D's need without further dispute.
Agent C: raised an adjacent-seat/aisle concern but did not press a competing claim or change position; no substantive role in resolution.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'that's my seat... I need four minutes to eat; will you move now...' vs Agent B: 'I see the tissue, but that doesn't give you priority... It'll take me about eight minutes; I won't move until it's empty.' Direct incompatible claims about who may occupy the seat now.

Agent A shortens acceptable wait ('can wait only two more') and demands 'What concrete accommodation will you make...' while Agent B has refused to yield. Agent C raises an additional practical concern (aisle narrowing), increasing stakes.

Agent D pressures B ('my meal's getting cold... can you hurry or set the bowl down?') and Agent B reiterates refusal to set down/leave until bowl is ~one-third full and demands ~three more minutes. Positions remain firm.

An alternative seat appears and is taken by D (reducing the number of people affected), but Agent A still requests exact timing and Agent B still occupies the disputed seat for several spoonfuls more. Disagreement persists but pressure on the group has eased.
Agent B: 'I'm done—leaving now. The seat's free for you.' Agent B leaves and Agent A takes the seat. The substantive dispute over seat occupation is settled by B vacating the seat.
Two minutes after the seat change there are no standing seat-seekers and no expressed disagreement; Agent A occupies the disputed seat and no conflict is visible.

substantive_insights: A visible placeholder (tissue packet) can be asserted as a claim but is contested and not universally accepted as creating priority.
A practical safety concern (risk of spilling an uncovered bowl) constrained B's ability to yield and justified B's firm refusal to temporarily vacate.
Arrival and occupation of an alternative seat by D reduced group pressure, but did not resolve the A–B incompatibility until B finished eating.
Resolution occurred via completion of the blocking condition (bowl emptied) rather than by negotiated time-sharing or a forced concession.
